slot.brief: Rank given elements by first ionisation enthalpy, exploiting the half-filled/filled orbital anomaly.

stem: Which one of the following represents the correct increasing order of first ionisation enthalpy of the elements N, O, F and Ne?

verdicts.working: O has lower first ionisation enthalpy than N because N has a half-filled 2p subshell. Across the period, values then increase: O < N < F < Ne.

working:
First ionisation enthalpy values: N = 1402 kJ mol^-1, O = 1314 kJ mol^-1, F = 1681 kJ mol^-1, Ne = 2080 kJ mol^-1. Oxygen has lower ionisation enthalpy than nitrogen because nitrogen has a stable half-filled 2p3 configuration and oxygen has electron-electron repulsion in the paired 2p orbital. Hence the correct increasing order is O < N < F < Ne.

Independent check: O has lower first ionisation enthalpy than N because N has a half-filled 2p subshell. Across the period, values then increase: O < N < F < Ne.
solution:
Across the period, first ionisation enthalpy generally increases. Nitrogen has a stable half-filled $2p^3$ subshell, so oxygen’s paired-electron repulsion makes its ionisation enthalpy lower.
$$\mathrm{O<N<F<Ne}$$
